//: Pins the .NET SDK, so the same source produces the same build everywhere.
This file exists because the build was NOT reproducible without it. The analyzer
set behind AnalysisLevel=latest-recommended is resolved by the SDK, and it changes
between feature bands: this solution compiled cleanly on 9.0.306 and failed on
9.0.316, where CA1716 is promoted and rejects the Domain type named Error. With
TreatWarningsAsErrors on and no pin, whether a clone builds depended on which SDK
the machine happened to have — the kind of failure that greets a new contributor
on their first clone and a release pipeline on its first upgraded runner.
The 9.x line, not 10.x, because the projects target net9.0 and the container runs
mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:9.0 — build, target, and runtime should agree.
Building net9.0 with the 10.x SDK is supported and works, but it puts the toolchain
that compiles the code a major version ahead of the one that runs it, and analyzer
drift like the above is part of what that costs.
rollForward latestFeature accepts any 9.0.x the machine has, so a routine patch
update does not break the build. It will NOT roll forward to 10.x: contributors need
a .NET 9 SDK. CI installs it from this file; the Dockerfile pins the matching image.
